A proposal · Three days · Two nights · One trailer

White Rock,
Black
Cinder

Two nights out, and the ground could not be more different. Night one on sandstone that set 190 million years ago. Night two on cinder that fell out of the sky less than a thousand years back. Same truck, same trailer, same ATV.

~650 mi round trip 2 nights on the ground $0 lodging 1 evening with Van

The shape of it / schematic, not to scale

Straight up,
straight back
down

North on 89 to the sand for the first night, then one clean run south to the cinder fields outside Flagstaff for the second. Van meets us there.

Day 01 / Vermilion Cliffs National Monument

Ditch the truck
where the sand starts

Five hours of highway, then the pavement quits. We drop the trailer at the end of the good road, put the family on the ATV, and ride the last stretch into White Pocket — a few square miles of sandstone that looks like a frozen ocean. The ATV gets us there; the place itself we walk.

  • First lightOut early. The hike needs light at the far end.
  • +5 hrsHouse Rock Valley Road. Park where the sand gets serious.
  • MiddayRide in and set camp on the slickrock.
  • 2+ hrsOn foot through the swirls, pools and fins. None of it is visible from a seat.
  • SunsetDinner outside. The rock turns orange, then violet.
  • DarkNo town for 40 miles. That's the whole point.
Drive5hrs
Elevation4,900ft
On foot2+hrs
PermitNone
Why this spot White Pocket needs no lottery permit — unlike The Wave next door, which almost nobody wins. The catch is the road instead: deep, soft sand that eats stock trucks. The ATV is what makes this day work.
Pack it in No water, no toilets, no cell service. Everything we drink and cook comes with us, and everything else comes back out.

Day 01 · after dark / White Pocket, Vermilion Cliffs

This is what
we're camping on

A few square miles of Navajo sandstone that buckled and swirled before it ever set — white, rust and pink stacked in ribbons, with rain pools caught in the hollows. No permit, no crowd, no lights. We put camp on the slickrock and watch it go dark.

Photos: Bureau of Land Management, public domain · night sky by John Fowler, CC BY 2.0

Day 02 / Cinder Hills OHV Area · Coconino National Forest

Load the ATV,
drive to the black stuff

Breakfast on the slickrock, ride out to the truck, and put the machine back on the trailer. Three hours south and the ground turns from white sandstone to black volcanic cinder — thirteen thousand acres of it, open to ride.

  • SunriseBreakfast at camp. Ride out and load the trailer.
  • +3 hrsSouth on 89 past Cameron. Ponderosa starts as the rim comes up.
  • AfternoonPick a spot in the cinders and set up. Van drives out to meet us.
  • EveningRide the cones until the light goes. Fire, dinner, a lot of sky.
Drive3hrs
Elevation7,000ft
Riding13,000acres
Nights1
Van's invitation It's about forty minutes from town, so Van can drive out for the afternoon and head home after dinner — or throw a bag in the truck and camp with us. Either way we get the whole evening.
Nothing like day one Cinder is a completely different surface from sandstone: soft, loose and deep, with cones to climb and berms that move under you. Same machine, two entirely different days of riding.

Day 02 · the other ground / Cinder Hills, Coconino National Forest

Ground that fell
out of the sky
a thousand
years ago

Sunset Crater blew around 1085 and buried this country in black cinder — the Sinagua farming here watched it happen. What's left is thirteen thousand acres of the softest riding surface in Arizona, forty minutes from Van's front door.

Photos: Ken Thomas, public domain · Nhartmannphotos, CC BY 4.0 · James St. John, CC BY 2.0

Day 03 / Flagstaff and home

Breakfast with Van,
then downhill

No rush on the last day. Pack up slow, run into Flagstaff for a real meal with Van, and then the easy drop off the Mogollon Rim — six thousand feet down in ninety minutes.

  • MorningBreak camp. Hose the cinder off everything later.
  • Late AMBreakfast in Flagstaff — time with Van that isn't a parking lot.
  • AfternoonSouth on 17. Driveway by mid-afternoon.
Drive2.5hrs
Descent5,900ft
Total miles~650
Days off3
What it costs Both nights are dispersed camping on public land — BLM at White Pocket, national forest at Cinder Hills. No reservations, no fees, nothing to book. The entire trip is food and gas.

So

Three days.
Two nights.
In?

One night on white sandstone with nobody around for forty miles, one night on black cinder with Van, and home by mid-afternoon on the third day. No rooms to book and nothing to reserve — just food and gas. Say the word and I'll pick a weekend.
